function.one_sentence_plain_english: A single LED bulb that has three tiny colored lights, red, green, and blue, built into one clear or frosted dome, so one part can glow almost any color.
function.what_it_is_used_for: Used in Arduino projects to create custom multi-colored or animated lighting effects, such as mood lighting, status indicators, or simple color displays, using one component instead of three separate single-color LEDs.
function.how_it_works_briefly: Inside the dome are three separate tiny LED chips, one red, one green, one blue, that all share one common ground leg (this part is the common cathode type, meaning that shared leg is the negative side). Sending a rapidly pulsing signal (PWM, or pulse width modulation) of different average brightness to each of the three color legs mixes the light your eye sees into a wide range of colors, similar to how a TV or phone screen mixes red, green, and blue dots.

pins.pin_1_identification: Looking at the dome from the front with the four leads pointing down, the order is R, common cathode, G, B. The common cathode lead is reliably identified as the single longest lead of the four, use that rather than position alone, since leads are sometimes trimmed or bent during use.

electrical.operating_voltage: Each color die has its own forward voltage rather than one shared supply voltage: red approximately 2.0 V typical, green approximately 3.2 V typical, blue approximately 3.2 V typical, at rated forward current
electrical.absolute_max_voltage: Not confirmed from a fetched source, treat the typical forward voltage per color as the practical limit and always use a series resistor
electrical.max_current: 20 mA per color channel per the sourced reference datasheet, a separate absolute-maximum current rating distinct from this typical value was not confirmed
electrical.logic_level: Not a logic input. Each color leg is driven from a 5V Arduino digital or PWM output through its own series resistor

key_specs.lens_type: Clear or lightly diffused dome, exact finish of the ELEGOO-bundled part not confirmed

visual_identification.shape_and_size: Standard 5 mm dome-shaped LED bulb, the same overall size as a single-color 5mm LED, but with 4 leads instead of the usual 2
visual_identification.color_and_markings: The dome is usually clear or lightly frosted/diffused plastic rather than tinted red, green, or blue, because it must emit all three colors. No part number or markings are printed on the LED body itself
visual_identification.printed_text_to_look_for: None expected, this type of LED is not laser-marked. Identify it by counting 4 leads and noting one leg is longer than the other three, not by text
easily_confused_with: 4-lead bi-color LEDs (also 4 leads but only 2 colors, not 3)
IR receiver modules (3 leads, different flatter shape)

required_extra_parts: One current-limiting resistor per color leg (commonly 220 ohm for 5V logic, the exact value used in ELEGOO's own tutorial could not be confirmed)
wiring_to_uno.arduino_library: None required, driven with the built-in analogWrite() function on PWM-capable pins

hazards: Very low voltage and current, not a shock or burn hazard
Looking directly into the lit LED at very close range can be uncomfortably bright, especially the blue die, avoid staring straight into it
handling_notes: Never wire a color leg directly across 5V and GND without a series resistor, the LED die will be damaged or burn out almost instantly
Bend leads gently, repeated sharp bending at the base of a lead can crack the internal wire bond
Static discharge is not a significant concern for this simple LED
common_mistakes: Wiring it as if it only needed one resistor like a single-color LED, each of the 3 color legs needs its own resistor
Reversing which leg is the common leg, causing no color, or the wrong combination of colors, to light
Connecting the common leg to 5V instead of GND, this part is common cathode so the common leg must go to GND, not 5V
Miscounting legs after they have been trimmed short, losing the longest-leg cue used to find the common pin

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: No colors light up at all
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: Common leg is not connected to GND, or is connected to 5V instead, which is backwards for this common-cathode part
symptoms_and_causes.check: Verify the longest leg goes to GND, move it there if it was on 5V

symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: A resistor or jumper wire is missing or loose on one or more color legs, or that pin is not being driven in the sketch
symptoms_and_causes.check: Use a multimeter to check continuity from the Arduino pin through the resistor to the LED leg, and confirm the sketch writes to that pin

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: Colors look dim or washed out
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: Resistor value is too high, or the PWM duty cycle in the sketch is too low
symptoms_and_causes.check: Measure voltage across the LED leg while PWM is active, and compare the resistor's value to the typical 220 ohm reference

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: One color is noticeably dimmer than the others at the same PWM level
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: Different color dies have different forward voltages, red is lower than green or blue, so identical resistors make red appear brighter or dimmer than the others depending on wiring
symptoms_and_causes.check: This can be normal behavior, try a different resistor value on the mismatched color leg to balance perceived brightness

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: Set the multimeter to diode-test mode. Put the black (COM) probe on the longest leg (the common cathode) and touch the red probe to each of the other three legs in turn. Each color die should light dimly and the meter should show a forward-voltage-like reading, red typically the lowest, green and blue typically similar and a bit higher. If a color die does not light during this test, that die is likely damaged or that leg was misidentified.

confidence.notes: ELEGOO's own product page and blog tutorial both returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches, and the official tutorial PDF exceeded the fetch tool's size limit, so the ELEGOO-specific manual could not be directly confirmed within budget. Pin order (R, common cathode/GND as the longest leg, G, B) and common-cathode polarity are corroborated by two independently fetched sources (components101.com and SparkFun) and match the seed guess, so confidence in the pinout itself is reasonably solid. Exact manufacturer, MPN, absolute maximum ratings, and the precise resistor value ELEGOO's own tutorial specifies are not confirmed and are treated as generic/typical values for this component class rather than ELEGOO-verified specifics. The unit price ($2.30) is SparkFun's price for its own individual RGB LED product (COM-00105), used as a generic single-unit reference retail price since ELEGOO does not sell this LED separately outside the kit bundle.
